$comment: Generated from the tool definitions of the Emelia MCP server. Do not edit by hand.

server.name: emelia
server.title: Emelia
server.description: Cold email and LinkedIn outreach: campaigns, lists, enrichment, LinkedIn extractions, warmup, inbox.

toolsets.title: Campaigns
toolsets.summary: Campaigns, their sequence and its guide, the contacts of a campaign, statistics and activities, manual tasks, attachments and voice notes.

toolsets.title: Enrichment
toolsets.summary: Find an email or a phone number, verify an email.

toolsets.title: LinkedIn scraper
toolsets.summary: Sales Navigator and LinkedIn search extractions, and the LinkedIn accounts that run them.

toolsets.title: Inbox
toolsets.summary: Read, search, sort, reply to and send the emails of the inbox.

toolsets.title: Inbox settings
toolsets.summary: Labels, AI label rules, views, inbox filters, auto-forward rules.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List all campaigns of the Emelia account (multichannel: email + LinkedIn steps in one campaign), with their id, name and status.

tools.name: get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign details
tools.description: Get the full configuration of a campaign: status, schedule, steps, and the contact lists attached to it (recipients.lists) or excluded from it (recipients.excludedLists), each with id, name and contact count. To manage the contacts of an attached list (add, update, search, delete), use the list tools with the list id.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.title: Create a campaign
tools.description: Create a new draft campaign with the given name. The campaign is created empty: set its sequence with update_campaign_steps, its schedule with update_campaign_settings, its sending identities with update_campaign_identities and its contact lists with update_campaign_recipients, then start it with start_campaign. Attach contacts by adding them to a list that the campaign uses.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Campaign name

tools.name: get_campaign_stats
tools.title: Get campaign statistics
tools.description: Get the statistics of a campaign: global metrics (sent, opens, clicks, replies, bounces...) and a breakdown per step. Optionally restrict to a date range with start/end (ISO dates).

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID

parameters.name: detailed
parameters.description: Include detailed statistics

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start date (ISO 8601) to filter the stats

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End date (ISO 8601) to filter the stats

notes: `end` is an exact bound: a date without a time excludes that day.
On an unknown campaign id the error reads like refused credentials ("Emelia refused the credentials of this connection"). Check the campaign id first.

tools.name: get_campaign_activities
tools.title: Get campaign activities
tools.description: Get the activity feed of a campaign (sent, opened, clicked, replied, bounced, LinkedIn events...). Replied activities include the reply content. Filter by activity type or contact.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by activity type (e.g. REPLIED, OPENED, SENT)

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Filter by contact ID

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: Filter by A/B version ID

notes: Returns the most recent page only (30 activities). For the full history, use `export_campaign`.

Main `type` values: `SENT`, `OPENED`, `CLICKED`, `MAIL_REPLIED`, `BOUNCED`, `UNSUBSCRIBED`, `VISITED`, `INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `MESSAGE_SENT`, `INMAIL_SENT`, `LINKEDIN_REPLIED`, `WHATSAPP_REPLIED`, `TASK_COMPLETED`, `TASK_FAILED`. For replies, use `MAIL_REPLIED` or `LINKEDIN_REPLIED` (not `REPLIED`).

tools.name: list_manual_tasks
tools.title: List pending manual tasks
tools.description: List the pending manual tasks of a campaign (steps that require a human action, e.g. a LinkedIn touch done by hand). Each task carries the contact, the step id (taskId) and its name.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID

parameters.name: stepId
parameters.description: Filter tasks by step ID

tools.name: complete_manual_task
tools.title: Set a manual task status
tools.description: Mark a pending manual task as completed ('ok') or failed ('ko') for a contact in a campaign.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign ID

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Contact ID

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The step ID of the manual task

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: 'ok' = completed, 'ko' = failed

tools.name: delete_campaign
tools.title: Delete a campaign
tools.description: Deletes the campaign. A running campaign must be paused first (pause_campaign). Its lists and contacts are kept. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: rename_campaign
tools.title: Rename a campaign
tools.description: Renames the campaign. Not allowed while the campaign is RUNNING.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: New campaign name

tools.name: get_campaign_sequence_guide
tools.title: Guide to campaign sequences
tools.description: How to write the steps of a campaign for update_campaign_steps: the step tree, step types, A/B versions versus successive messages, conditions, variables, attachments and voice notes, and how to edit a campaign that already sent. Read it before building or changing a sequence.

tools.name: update_campaign_steps
tools.title: Replace the sequence
tools.description: Replace the WHOLE sequence of a campaign. Read get_campaign_sequence_guide before building or changing a sequence: it explains step types, versions, conditions, variables and attachments. Rules that break a campaign: the root is always the START step ({ "_id": "START", "stepType": "START" }); read the current tree with get_campaign, change it and send it back whole; leave _id out on new steps and versions and keep the existing ids untouched, or contacts receive steps again; the campaign must not be RUNNING (pause_campaign first). Content is only checked by start_campaign.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: One node of the sequence tree. The root is always a `START` step. Each node points to the next one with `next`; a `CONDITION` node branches with `yes` and `no` (a missing branch ends the sequence for the contacts that fall into it). `END_OF_CAMPAIGN` stops the sequence. EMAIL versions are A/B variants (one version per contact); MESSAGE and WHATSAPP versions are successive messages sent in order. A MESSAGE step placed after a CONNECTION step waits for the invitation to be accepted.

notes: Replaces the whole tree. Read `get_campaign_sequence_guide` first: a wrong step id makes contacts receive steps again.

tools.name: update_campaign_settings
tools.title: Update campaign settings
tools.description: Merges the given settings into the campaign schedule. Not allowed while RUNNING. Rules: `start` must be before `end`; `dailyEmailLimit` must be greater than or equal to `dailyEmailAdded`; `dailyLinkedinAdded` is capped at 40 when the sequence contains a CONNECTION step (80 otherwise). Returns the updated campaign.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.description: Settings to merge into the campaign schedule. `trackLinks`, `trackOpens`, `blacklistUnsub`, `start` and `end` are always required. Send the full object you read with get_campaign (field `schedule`).

tools.name: update_campaign_recipients
tools.title: Set the contact lists of a campaign
tools.description: Sets the FULL selection of lists (replace semantics): the campaign contacts become the contacts of `lists`, minus any contact whose email or LinkedIn URL appears in one of `excludedLists`. When `excludedLists` is omitted the current exclusion lists are kept. Allowed on a running campaign. A campaign cannot be started with more than 30,000 recipients. Create and fill lists with the list tools (create_list, add_contact_to_list, add_contacts_to_list_bulk).

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: lists
parameters.description: Ids of the lists to use.

parameters.name: excludedLists
parameters.description: Ids of exclusion lists.

tools.name: update_campaign_identities
tools.title: Set the sender identities
tools.description: Replaces the identities (sending accounts) of the campaign. Not allowed while RUNNING. For each step Emelia picks automatically, among these identities, the least used one that has an account on the channel. Rules checked at start: every identity needs an email provider if the sequence has an email step; with a LinkedIn step either use a single LinkedIn account or attach one to every identity.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: identities
parameters.description: `name` is required and at least one of `email`, `linkedin`, `whatsapp`. Duplicated accounts are silently dropped. Accounts that do not belong to you are rejected.

tools.name: schedule_campaign_start
tools.title: Schedule or cancel a planned start
tools.description: Schedules an automatic start at `plannedStart` (ISO 8601 date in the future). The campaign must pass the start checks at scheduling time (same errors as start_campaign). Send `null` (or an empty value) to cancel a planned start.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: plannedStart
parameters.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the start, or `null` to cancel the planned start.

tools.name: duplicate_campaign
tools.title: Duplicate a campaign
tools.description: Creates a new DRAFT campaign from an existing one. Choose what to copy. Copied contacts and lists are shared references (not copies). The new name must be unique.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the new campaign

parameters.name: copySettings
parameters.description: Copy the settings (default false)

parameters.name: copySteps
parameters.description: Copy the sequence (default false)

parameters.name: copyContacts
parameters.description: Copy the contacts and lists (default false)

parameters.name: copyIdentities
parameters.description: Copy the sender identities (default false)

tools.name: start_campaign
tools.title: Start a campaign
tools.description: Starts sending to the real contacts of the campaign: confirm with the user before calling it. Starts (or resumes) the campaign. Requires an active subscription. All start checks are run and the first failing one is returned with a stable `code` (for example `NO_IDENTITY_SET`, `EMAIL_VERSION_NO_SUBJECT`, `NO_RECIPIENTS`, `RECIPIENTS_NO_EMAIL`): identities, accounts connected, email versions with content and subject, LinkedIn daily ceiling, 1 to 30,000 recipients, at least one contact reachable on each channel used. A planned start, if any, is cancelled. Scheduling of contacts happens asynchronously after the response.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

notes: Not flagged as destructive, but it sends to the real contacts of the campaign.

tools.name: pause_campaign
tools.title: Pause a campaign
tools.description: Pauses a RUNNING campaign: its scheduled actions, pending conditions and pending manual tasks are deleted. They are created again when the campaign is restarted and the contacts reach those steps again.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: archive_campaign
tools.title: Archive a campaign
tools.description: Sets the status to ARCHIVED (hidden from list_campaigns). A running campaign must be paused first (pause_campaign).

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: reactivate_campaign
tools.title: Reactivate a finished campaign
tools.description: Moves a FINISHED campaign back to PAUSED so that it can be edited and started again.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: finish_campaign
tools.title: Mark a campaign as finished
tools.description: Moves a RUNNING or PAUSED campaign to FINISHED and deletes its scheduled actions and pending conditions.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: send_campaign_test_email
tools.title: Send a test email
tools.description: Sends a real email to the given address. Sends one version of an EMAIL step to `email`, from one of the campaign identities, with the variables of a random contact of the campaign. Use the step `_id` and version `_id` from get_campaign.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: stepId
parameters.description: `_id` of the EMAIL step

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: `_id` of the version to send

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Recipient of the test.

notes: Not flagged as destructive, but it sends a real email.

tools.name: list_campaign_contacts
tools.title: List the contacts of a campaign
tools.description: Paginated contacts of a campaign with their status in the campaign. `page` is ZERO based: the first page is 0, the default. `perPage` below 10 is replaced by 20; maximum 10,000.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign id.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Zero based page index: the first page is 0 (default 0).

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Page size (default 20).

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Filter on contact status (for example `SENT`, `MAIL_REPLIED`; `NO_ACTIVITY` = no activity yet). One status or several.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Exact email, or words matched against email, names, phone and LinkedIn URL.

tools.name: add_contact_to_campaign
tools.title: Add a contact to a campaign
tools.description: Adds ONE contact to a multichannel campaign. The contact is stored in a list named "<campaign name> contacts from API" (created if needed) attached to the campaign. If the campaign is FINISHED it is started again automatically (all start checks apply); if it is RUNNING the contact is scheduled immediately. A contact already present in that list (same email or LinkedIn URL) is rejected. For many contacts, use the list tools (add_contacts_to_list_bulk) and update_campaign_recipients instead.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign id.

parameters.name: contact
parameters.description: Contact to add. At least one of `email` or `linkedinUrlProfile`. Only `email`, `linkedinUrlProfile`, `phone`, `firstName` and `lastName` are stored as native fields; every other key becomes a custom variable usable as `{{key}}` in messages. ALL VALUES MUST BE STRINGS: a number, an object or an array makes the whole request fail with a 400 error. Empty strings are ignored.

tools.name: remove_contact_from_campaign
tools.title: Remove a contact from a campaign
tools.description: Removes one contact from the campaign recipients and deletes its activities in this campaign (in the background). The contact itself and its lists are kept. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign id.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Contact ID (`_id` from list_campaign_contacts).

tools.name: set_campaign_contact_field
tools.title: Set a field on a campaign contact
tools.description: Sets one field of a contact that belongs to the campaign, found by `email` OR `linkedinUrlProfile` (exactly one of them). Spaces are removed from `fieldName`. If `fieldName` is a native field of the contact (for example `firstName`, `jobTitle`, `companyName`) it is overwritten, otherwise a custom variable is created or updated.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Campaign id.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email of the contact (or linkedinUrlProfile, not both).

parameters.name: linkedinUrlProfile
parameters.description: LinkedIn profile URL of the contact (or email, not both).

parameters.name: fieldName
parameters.description: Field or custom variable to set.

parameters.name: fieldValue
parameters.description: New value.

tools.name: get_activity_message
tools.title: Get the message of a send activity
tools.description: Rebuilds the content sent for a `SENT`, `MESSAGE_SENT`, `INMAIL_SENT`, `INVITED` or `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_SENT` activity by replaying the step template against the contact. The sent content itself is not stored: the result can differ if the step or the contact changed since. Errors use a different format here: `{"error": "NOT_FOUND"}` (404) or `{"error": "NO_MESSAGE"}` (422).

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: activityId
parameters.description: Activity id (`_id` from get_campaign_activities).

tools.name: get_campaign_progress
tools.title: Get per step progress
tools.description: For each step id: how many contacts already passed the step (`completed`) and how many are currently waiting at it (`waiting`). Works on paused campaigns. Returns `{}` for a DRAFT or unknown campaign.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

tools.name: list_step_contacts
tools.title: List the contacts of a step
tools.description: Contacts that passed (`completed`) or wait at (`waiting`) a given step, newest first, 20 per page. Here `page` is ONE based.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: stepId
parameters.description: Step `_id` (from get_campaign or get_campaign_progress).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Default `all`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One based page index (default 1).

tools.name: export_campaign
tools.title: Export campaign data as CSV
tools.description: Returns campaign data as CSV text. `contacts`: one line per contact with its custom fields, activities and replied flag; `activities`: activity log; `replies`: replies. Optional date range on activities. A CSV longer than 100,000 characters is cut on a line boundary, with a note giving the number of lines shown.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of a multichannel campaign (24 hexadecimal characters), as returned by create_campaign or list_campaigns.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: What to export.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the date range on activities (ISO 8601 date-time).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End of the date range on activities (ISO 8601 date-time).

notes: The CSV is cut at 100,000 characters on a line boundary, with a note that gives the number of lines shown.

tools.name: upload_campaign_attachments
tools.title: Upload message attachments
tools.description: Uploads 1 to 3 files (20 MB maximum each) and returns their URLs, to reference in `versions[].attachments` of EMAIL, MESSAGE or WHATSAPP steps (update_campaign_steps). Files are stored as is with a PUBLIC URL: anyone with the URL can download them. The MCP request is limited to 4 MB, so about 3 MB of file once encoded in base64.

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: The files to upload, 1 to 3.

notes: Requests to the server are limited to 4 MB: about 3 MB of file per call, sent in base64.

tools.name: upload_linkedin_voice_note
tools.title: Upload a LinkedIn voice note
tools.description: Converts an audio file (webm expected, 10 MB maximum, 5 minutes maximum) to m4a and returns a PUBLIC URL plus its duration IN MILLISECONDS, to use as an attachment with `mediaType: "AUDIO"` in a MESSAGE step (update_campaign_steps). Anyone with the URL can download it. The MCP request is limited to 4 MB, so about 3 MB of file once encoded in base64.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.description: The recording to upload.

notes: Requests to the server are limited to 4 MB: about 3 MB of file per call, sent in base64.

tools.name: create_list
tools.title: Create a list
tools.description: Create an empty contact list. Then add contacts with add_contact_to_list or add_contacts_to_list_bulk. Attach the list to a campaign with update_campaign_recipients to have its contacts flow into the campaign automatically.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: List name

tools.name: list_lists
tools.title: List all lists
tools.description: List the contact lists of the account, with pagination, name search and filters. Lists created by a LinkedIn scrape appear here too (filter with source). Returns each list with its id, name and contact counters.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 25)

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search on list name

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter by import source

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by list status

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated tag IDs

tools.name: get_list
tools.title: Get list details
tools.description: Get a list by id: name, contact counters (leads, emails, phones, linkedins), source and status.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

tools.name: rename_list
tools.title: Rename a list
tools.description: Rename a list.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: New name

tools.name: delete_list
tools.title: Delete a list
tools.description: Permanently delete a list AND all its contacts. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

notes: Deletes every contact of the list for good.

tools.name: get_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts of a list
tools.description: Paginated listing of the contacts of a list. To check whether a specific contact exists (and get its leadId for update/delete), pass email or linkedinUrl instead: it returns the exact matches only. email and linkedinUrl are mutually exclusive and take precedence over search/pagination.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact contact lookup by email (case-insensitive)

parameters.name: linkedinUrl
parameters.description: Exact contact lookup by LinkedIn profile URL

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1)

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, max 100)

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Field to sort by

tools.name: get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Get a single contact of a list by its leadId (returned by add_contact_to_list or the email/linkedinUrl lookup of get_list_contacts).

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: leadId
parameters.description: Contact (lead) ID

tools.name: add_contact_to_list
tools.title: Add a contact to a list
tools.description: Add a single contact to a list. If the list is used by one or several campaigns, the contact automatically enters those campaigns; this is the standard way to feed a running campaign. Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. Duplicates (same email or LinkedIn URL already in the list) are not re-created: the response returns the existing leadId with duplicate: true. Set updateIfExists to true to update the existing contact instead (add-or-update).

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: contact
parameters.description: The contact fields, flat key → value

parameters.name: updateIfExists
parameters.description: Update the existing contact when a duplicate is found

notes: Contact fields are a flat object: standard fields (`firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `phone`, `linkedinUrlProfile`, `jobTitle`), company fields (`companyName`, `websiteUrl`) or your custom variables.

tools.name: add_contacts_to_list_bulk
tools.title: Add contacts in bulk
tools.description: Add up to 100 contacts to a list in one call (same behavior as add_contact_to_list for each row: campaign propagation, duplicate detection, updateIfExists). Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. Rows are processed independently; the response reports created/duplicates/updated/failed counts and a per-row result.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: contacts
parameters.description: The contacts, one flat object each (max 100)

parameters.name: updateIfExists
parameters.description: Update existing contacts when duplicates are found

notes: Loading 1,000 contacts is 10 calls of 100, not 1,000 single calls.

tools.name: update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: Update a contact by its leadId (its list is derived automatically). Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. The fields you send overwrite the contact's values; fields you don't send stay untouched. If the contact's list is used by campaigns, the updated values are propagated to them.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Contact (lead) ID

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The fields to update, flat key → value

tools.name: delete_contact
tools.title: Delete a contact
tools.description: Permanently delete a contact from a list (and its company data). If the list is used by campaigns, the contact is also removed from those campaigns. Cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it. Find the leadId with the email/linkedinUrl lookup of get_list_contacts.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List ID

parameters.name: leadId
parameters.description: Contact (lead) ID

notes: Deletes the contact for good and removes it from its campaigns.

tools.name: find_contact
tools.title: Find a contact across all lists
tools.description: Search a contact across ALL the lists of the account by email address or LinkedIn profile URL. Returns the lists that contain the contact and the contact data itself. Use this to answer "do we already have this person?" or to locate a contact before updating or deleting it.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Email address or LinkedIn profile URL

tools.name: find_campaigns_using_lists
tools.title: Find the campaigns using lists
tools.description: For each list id, returns the non-archived campaigns that include the list in their recipients. Use it to know whether adding contacts to a list will feed a campaign. Lists used only as exclusion lists are not reported. Ids that are not valid ObjectIds are dropped; ids of lists that are not yours return an empty array.

parameters.name: listIds
parameters.description: List ids (from list_lists).

tools.name: export_list
tools.title: Export a list as CSV
tools.description: Exports one list as CSV text and waits for the file. Columns: First Name, Last Name, Full Name, Email, Phone, Mobile Phone, Job Title, LinkedIn URL, Bio, Company, Website, LinkedIn Page, Company Size, Industry, Country, Region, City, Status, Handle, then one column per custom variable of the account, then Lists and Campaigns (company-only lists use a shorter header). `leadIds`, `search`, `statuses` and `filters` narrow the export. Up to 5,000 contacts the file comes back directly; above that Emelia prepares it in the background and this tool waits for it (up to 90 seconds), then returns the CSV. If it is still running after that, it returns the job id: call get_list_export later. Only one large export runs at a time per account: while one is queued or running, a new request returns that existing job, which may concern other lists. An export above 100,000 contacts is refused. Output beyond 100,000 characters is cut on a line boundary.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: List identifier, as returned by create_list or list_lists.

parameters.name: leadIds
parameters.description: Export only these contacts.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Same as `search` of get_list_contacts.

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Engagement statuses, `NO_ACTIVITY` included.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Column filters.

notes: One large export runs at a time per account: while it runs, a new request returns that job, which may concern other lists.
The CSV is cut at 100,000 characters on a line boundary, with a note that gives the number of lines shown.

tools.name: get_list_export
tools.title: Get a list export
tools.description: Reads an export started by export_list that was still running. While it runs, returns its progress (status queued, running, done or failed, rows written, total). Once done, returns the CSV file. A failed job reports its error: start the export again. Jobs are kept 24 hours; an unknown or expired job id returns an error. Output beyond 100,000 characters is cut on a line boundary.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Export job id (UUID) returned by export_list when the export is still running. Jobs are kept 24 hours.

tools.name: create_custom_variable
tools.title: Create a custom variable
tools.description:
Declares a custom variable on the account, so that contact keys with this name (technical or display name) land in it instead of being guessed. Declare your variables before loading contacts. This is the only way to create a COMPANY custom variable: add_contact_to_list and add_contacts_to_list_bulk only create contact (`lead`) variables.

Naming rule: a technical name that is already a clean identifier (letter first, then letters, digits or `_`) is kept, with its first letter lowercased (`basile_gmb_name` stays `basile_gmb_name`). Anything else is camelCased with accents and symbols dropped (`Ice breaker` becomes `iceBreaker`). The stored name is returned.

The call is refused (422) when a variable with the same name already exists for this schema (comparison ignoring case, spaces, `_` and `-`) or when the name is a standard field of the schema: it is therefore safe to call it every time and treat 422 as already existing. Variables are shared by all your lists and cannot be renamed or deleted through the API.

tools.name: list_linkedin_scrapers
tools.title: List your LinkedIn scrapers
tools.description:
Returns the scrapers of your workspace, newest first, 20 per page. Deleted scrapers are not returned.

Use it to show a history or to find a scraper id. To follow one extraction, poll get_linkedin_scraper instead: it is lighter and returns the same object.

For running segmented scrapers (large searches split into chunks, Grow and Scale plans), two computed fields are added: `nextRunningSegment` (when the next chunk is scheduled) and `betweenSegment` (true when no chunk is being extracted right now).

Pitfall: each object also contains internal fields not described here (cursors, legacy ids). Do not rely on them.

tools.name: get_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Get one LinkedIn scraper (poll its progress)
tools.description:
Returns one scraper with its progress. This is the call to poll while an extraction or an enrichment runs (every 30 to 60 seconds is enough).

**Reading the progress**
- `status`: see `ScrapperStatus`. The extraction is over when `status` is `done`; `error` gives the reason when `status` is `error`.
- `scrapIndex` contacts extracted out of `totalContact` (0 until LinkedIn reports the result count, then capped by the plan rules).
- Segmented searches: `segments`, `estimatedEnd`, `nextRunningSegment`, `betweenSegment`.
- After enrich_linkedin_scraper: `status` is `enriching`, then `done` again. `enrichIndex` and `enrichFound` are only filled at the end of the enrichment.
- `convertedListId`: id of the Emelia list automatically created from a finished scraper (usually within a few minutes after `done`), `null` before.

Unlike list_linkedin_scrapers, this response also contains `userId`.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: create_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Create a LinkedIn scraper (start an extraction)
tools.description:
Starts extracting the people (or companies) of a LinkedIn search into a CSV. The extraction runs in the background on Emelia servers: this call only creates the scraper and returns its id (`scrapId`). Follow it with get_linkedin_scraper or with a webhook (add_linkedin_scraper_webhook).

**Accepted URLs and accounts**
- Sales Navigator people search (`https://www.linkedin.com/sales/search/people...`), lead list (`.../sales/lists/people/...`) or account search (`.../sales/search/company...`, companies instead of people). `authes` must contain ids of LinkedIn accounts connected for scraping (the `authId` returned by connect_linkedin_scraper_account).
- Classic LinkedIn people search (`https://www.linkedin.com/search/results/people/...`). It runs on a LinkedIn account connected for campaigns: `authes` must contain ids of LinkedIn accounts connected for campaigns, not of accounts connected for scraping.
- Any other `https://linkedin.com/sales/...` URL is accepted here but the scraper then stops with the error `BAD_SALES_NAV_URL`.

**Volume limits** (applied during the extraction, not at creation)
- Sales Navigator never returns more than 2,500 results per search (100 pages of 25). Lead lists and saved searches are capped at 2,500, searches filtered on your network (`CONNECTION_OF`) at 1,000, account searches at 1,000 companies, classic searches at 1,000 people.
- Grow and Scale plans: a search with 3,000 results or more that contains filters is split automatically into chunks of at most 2,500 (`segmented: true`) and extracted over several days, at 2,500 contacts per day per LinkedIn account (5,000 for an account with a Sales Navigator Advanced seat). Give several accounts in `authes` to go faster. Above 80,000 results the scraper stops with `TOO_MUCH_RESULT`.
- Start plan and free use: capped at 2,500, no automatic split.
- `max_contacts` stops the extraction early. On Sales Navigator it is applied per page of 25 (you can get up to 25 more) and it is ignored for segmented searches. On classic searches it is exact.

**Rules checked by this call**: the name is unique among your scrapers; with a single account and no `plannedStart`, that account must not already run a scraper; every account exists, belongs to you and is valid; `plannedStart` is at least one hour ahead; your workspace has an active subscription, or has not used its free extraction yet, or still has credits (without subscription, extraction costs about 1 credit per 2 contacts and pauses when credits run out). Fields not listed in the schema are rejected.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique among your scrapers. Keep it at 100 characters or less (the rename limit).

parameters.name: authes
parameters.description: LinkedIn account ids. Sales Navigator URL: ids of accounts connected for scraping (`authId` returned by connect_linkedin_scraper_account). Classic search URL: ids of the LinkedIn accounts connected to your campaigns. All must be valid and yours. Several accounts share the chunks of a segmented extraction; otherwise one of them is picked at random.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Sales Navigator people search, lead list or account search URL, or classic LinkedIn people search URL, copied from the browser address bar.

parameters.name: plannedStart
parameters.description: Optional ISO 8601 start date, at least one hour ahead. The scraper stays `planified` until then.

parameters.name: max_contacts
parameters.description: Optional maximum number of contacts. Approximate on Sales Navigator (page of 25), ignored on segmented extractions, exact on classic searches.

notes: Without an Emelia subscription, the extraction uses credits: about 1 credit per 2 contacts, and it pauses when the credits run out.

tools.name: rename_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Rename a LinkedIn scraper
tools.description:
Changes the name of a scraper. 1 to 100 characters, unique among your scrapers.

Pitfall: renaming a scraper to its current name is refused (`A scrap with this name already exists`).

tools.name: delete_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Delete a LinkedIn scraper
tools.description:
Deletes a scraper. It disappears from the API and from the app. A Sales Navigator extraction in progress is stopped and the next chunks of a segmented extraction do not start.

Pitfalls: the deletion is logical (Emelia keeps the extracted file). A classic LinkedIn search that is already extracting is not stopped: it runs to its end (and still sends its FINISHED webhook). The Emelia list created from the scraper (`convertedListId`) is not deleted. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: pause_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Pause a segmented extraction
tools.description:
Pauses a large extraction split into chunks (`segmented: true`, Grow and Scale plans). Only allowed while `status` is `running`. Other scrapers cannot be paused.

The pause is not immediate: the chunk being extracted goes to its end, only the next chunks are unscheduled. `status` becomes `paused`. Restart with resume_linkedin_scraper.

A scraper can also be paused by Emelia when it runs on credits (no subscription) and the credits run out.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: resume_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Resume a paused, scheduled or failed scraper
tools.description:
Restarts a scraper that is:
- `paused` (by you, or automatically when credits ran out);
- `planified`: it starts now instead of at `plannedStart`;
- in `error` with `INVALID_COOKIE` or `RATE_LIMIT`, once its LinkedIn account is valid again (refresh it first with update_linkedin_scraper_account, or reconnect the campaign account for a classic search).

Other error codes are final: create a new scraper. A segmented extraction restarts with its remaining chunks. For Sales Navigator, a `RATE_LIMIT` stop is retried automatically about 12 hours later.

Checks: an active subscription or remaining credits; no other running scraper on the same account.

Known issues: the running scraper check can refuse the resume with `You already have a running scrap` as soon as any other scraper of the workspace is running, even on another account. An unknown id is reported as `This scrap is in invalid state` (or as the running scraper message), not as not found.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: split_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Detach the part already extracted from a segmented extraction
tools.description:
Lets you use now what a long segmented extraction has already collected, while the rest goes on.

Effect: a new scraper named `<name> 1` is created with `status` `done` and the contacts extracted so far; its id is returned in `scrapId`. The original scraper keeps its id, is renamed `<name> 2`, keeps only the chunks not finished yet and restarts its counter (`scrapIndex` back to 0, `totalContact` reduced accordingly). The new part is then imported automatically into an Emelia list, like any finished scraper.

Typical use: enrich or download the first contacts of an extraction that will take days (enrichment requires `status` `done`).

Conditions: `segmented` is true, `status` is neither `enriching` nor `done`, at least one contact was extracted, and nothing was written during the last 10 minutes (otherwise retry later).

Not to be confused with the automatic split of large searches into chunks, which Emelia does by itself on Grow and Scale plans.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: filter_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Remove contacts already extracted by your other scrapers
tools.description:
Removes from this scraper the LinkedIn profiles that already appear in your 10 most recent finished scrapers (comparison on the profile `id` column). Run it on a finished scraper before enriching it: fewer contacts, fewer credits.

`filters` is a bit field. Only `1` exists today (remove profiles found in your other scrapers); use `1`.

Asynchronous: the call returns at once and sets `processing` to true on the scraper. When the filter ends, `processing` is false again and `totalContact` and `scrapIndex` give the new count. Large files can take several minutes.

Pitfalls: the CSV is rewritten and the previous version cannot be restored through the API. The filter is not restricted to finished scrapers: do not run it while an extraction is in progress. `filters: 0` is accepted but nothing runs and `processing` stays true.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Bit field. `1` = remove the profiles found in your 10 most recent finished scrapers. No other bit is implemented. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: enrich_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Find the emails of a finished scraper
tools.description:
Consumes credits. Looks for the professional email of every contact of a finished people extraction. Asynchronous: `status` becomes `enriching`, then `done` again when the emails are written into the CSV. An enrichment is closed after about one hour at most, with what was found by then.

**Credits**: you need at least as many credits as `totalContact`. That amount is taken when the enrichment starts, then the credits of the contacts without an email are given back at the end: you pay 1 credit per email found. Your balance therefore drops temporarily during the enrichment.

`country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (for example `FR`) used as a hint for the search. It is not validated.

Conditions: `status` is `done` and the scraper was never enriched (`enrichEnabled` false). To enrich the first part of a long segmented extraction, split it first (split_linkedin_scraper). Only for people searches: an account (company) search has no person to look up.

After completion: `enrichFound` is the number of emails found. Download with `format=1` to get only the contacts with an email, and read the columns `email_emelia`, `qualification_emelia`, `gender_emelia`, `domain_emelia`. No webhook is sent at the end of an enrichment: poll get_linkedin_scraper.

Phone number enrichment of a scraper is not available in this API.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the contacts, used as a hint (for example `FR`, `US`). Not validated.

notes: As many credits as the extraction has contacts are taken at the start; those of the contacts without an email come back at the end.

tools.name: download_linkedin_scraper
tools.title: Download the contacts of a scraper (CSV)
tools.description:
Returns the CSV of a scraper as text. Separator `;`, first line = column names, UTF-8 without BOM, values quoted only when needed. Large extractions give large responses; output beyond 100,000 characters is cut on a line boundary.

It can be called while the extraction runs: you get what has been collected so far.

`format`: `1` = only contacts with an email (requires a finished enrichment with at least one email), `2` = only contacts without an email (all contacts if the scraper was never enriched), `3` = all contacts.

**People columns** (Sales Navigator and classic searches): id, firstName, lastName, fullName, location, isPremium, openProfile, linkedinUrlProfile, summary, title, company, companyId, companyLocation, companyDescription, companySize, estimatedMinRevenue, estimatedMaxRevenue, industry, description, companyPage, companyWebsite, type. `id` is the Sales Navigator profile key and can contain commas. Fields that LinkedIn does not provide stay empty (classic searches fill fewer columns).

**After an email enrichment** the file is rewritten in this order: id, email_emelia, qualification_emelia, gender_emelia, firstName, lastName, fullName, location, isPremium, openProfile, linkedinUrlProfile, phone_number_emelia, phone_qualification_emelia, phone_country_emelia, summary, title, company, companyId, companyLocation, companyDescription, companySize, estimatedMaxRevenue, estimatedMinRevenue, industry, description, companyPage, companyWebsite, domain_emelia, type.

**Account search columns** (companies): id, companyName, companyPage, companyDescription, companySize, employeeCountRange, industry, companyWebsite, companyLocation, yearFounded, type, estimatedMinRevenue, estimatedMaxRevenue.

Once a scraper is `done`, its contacts are also imported automatically into an Emelia list (`convertedListId`), that you can manage with the list tools.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: 1 = contacts with an email only, 2 = contacts without an email only, 3 = all contacts.

notes: The CSV is cut at 100,000 characters on a line boundary, with a note that gives the number of lines shown.

tools.name: add_linkedin_scraper_webhook
tools.title: Register a webhook on a scraper
tools.description:
Registers a URL that Emelia calls when this scraper finishes or stops on an error. Register it right after creating the scraper. Several URLs can be registered on the same scraper; the same URL cannot be added twice.

**What is sent**: a `POST` with a JSON body `{ "event", "id", "name", "error" }` (see `ScrapperWebhookEvent`). `FINISHED` is sent when the extraction ends (`status` `done`, all chunks included). `ERROR` is sent when the scraper stops with an error code, at most once per hour for the same scraper and code.

**Current behavior to know**: every registered URL receives every event, whatever its `events` list; `ERROR` is only sent if at least one registered URL asked for `ERROR`. One attempt only: no retry, no signature, no custom header, so check the scraper with get_linkedin_scraper when you receive a call. Nothing is sent at the end of an enrichment.

`events` must contain `FINISHED` or `ERROR`; other values are accepted and ignored.

Known issue: the success response is currently an empty JSON object `{}` (no `success` field). Treat HTTP 200 as success.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Scraper id (`_id` returned by create_linkedin_scraper or list_linkedin_scrapers). 24 hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: webhookUrl
parameters.description: Public URL that accepts a POST with a JSON body.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: At least one of `FINISHED`, `ERROR`. Today every registered URL receives every event anyway.

tools.name: remove_linkedin_scraper_webhook
tools.title: Remove a webhook from a scraper
tools.description:
Unregisters a webhook URL (exact match). Removing a URL that is not registered is not an error.

tools.name: connect_linkedin_scraper_account
tools.title: Connect a LinkedIn account for scraping (session cookies)
tools.description:
Connects a LinkedIn account for Sales Navigator scraping by sending the cookies of a browser session where the user is logged in to LinkedIn and Sales Navigator. No password is involved. The Emelia browser extension does this for you; use this tool to automate it.

`li_at` is required. Strongly recommended: `li_a` (Sales Navigator session), `ua` (user agent of the browser the cookies come from), `additionnalsCookie` (the other linkedin.com cookies, as objects `{ name, value, domain }`), `viewport` (that browser window size) and `country` (ISO alpha-2 code: Emelia browses LinkedIn through a proxy located in this country; default the workspace country, then FR).

Returns `authId`, to use in `authes` of create_linkedin_scraper. The same `li_at` cannot be registered twice. When a session expires, update the existing account with update_linkedin_scraper_account instead of creating a new one.

Emelia stores these cookies and refreshes them after each scraping session. There is currently no tool to remove a connected scraping account.

Pitfall: `JSESSIONID` goes inside `additionnalsCookie`. Fields not described here are reserved for Emelia apps.

Then restart the stopped scraper with resume_linkedin_scraper.

Send the complete set every time: `li_a`, `ua`, `viewport`, `country` and `additionnalsCookie` that you omit are cleared, and so is the LinkedIn profile shown in the app.
